Elaine — thanks for the samples and the target date. I pulled together an initial MAP worksheet and a proposed evaluation plan (attached). High level plan below.

Plan summary (proposed):
- Week 1 (Sept 3-7): Align workload slices and acceptance criteria; share Redwood test harness and data format.
- Week 2 (Sept 8-11): Run directed benchmarks (latency/TTFT/throughput) across two model variants (rt-large, rt-medium) and two quantization profiles.
- Week 3 (Sept 14-16): Soak and spike tests to validate stability at target concurrency and fallback behavior.
- Sept 17: Go/no-go close based on acceptance gates in the MAP.

Success gates (draft):
- TTFT server-side p95 <= 1.2s for interactive slice (<= 1024 tokens).
- 99th token latency for streaming path under 200ms additional per-token overhead.
- Sustained throughput >= 250 req/s for batch slice (median payload size ~ 150 tokens) with <1% error rate.
- No regression in output quality vs baseline prompts (qualitative pass reviewed by Tom).

Deliverables we will provide: test harness, raw result CSVs, a short runbook with kernel/quantization settings. Please review the attached MAP workbook and the load_profile_v2.json — I matched the peaks you sent to a 2:1 peak:baseline model.

Marissa and Sergio are looped for ops and escalation if we hit capacity issues. If that looks good I will schedule a 30-min alignment tomorrow.

Best,
Rafael

Great call yesterday, all. Notes and a small change to the acceptance gates after discussing with infra:
- Interactive slice (web chat flows): target p50 TTFT <= 250ms, p95 <= 1.2s for short prompts (<=512 tokens). We will capture on-server metrics (request receive timestamp, model start, first-token) to avoid network noise.
- Streaming path: measure per-token delta; p95 per-token delta < 220ms when under target concurrency.
- Batch slice (async inference): sustained throughput target 260 req/s at median 140 tokens/request with p99 end-to-end <= 2.5s. Error rate <1%.
- Concurrency: ramp tests to 250 open streams, sustained soak at 150 for 30 minutes.

Test matrix will include: rt-large (fp16), rt-large-int8, rt-medium-int8. We will produce a normalized cost curve (tokens/sec per GPU and cost per 1M tokens).

Next steps: I asked our infra to run an initial directed benchmark on a representative bucket last night and share raw results this week. Sergio will own run coordination.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP: Sentinel Health - load profile, success gates & initial benchmark results

Elaine / Tom — sharing the initial directed-run summary we completed against their sample bucket. See attached CSV and short notes below.

Summary (directed run, 2026-09-07 22:00 UTC):
- Model: rt-large (fp16) on p4-equivalent nodes.
- Interactive slice (single-stream synthetic): p50 TTFT = 190ms, p95 TTFT = 1.05s, p99 = 1.6s.
- Streaming per-token delta: median 95ms, p95 210ms under 50 concurrent streams.
- Batch slice: sustained 275 req/s at median 140 tokens/request with p99 end-to-end = 2.3s.
- Concurrency soak: at 150 sustained streams for 30 minutes we saw stable GPU utilization ~68% and KV cache hit rate 41%. Error rate observed 0.4% (network retries).

Notes and caveats:
- The run used a sanitized sample set; real production prompts include a heavier tail of long-context examples which will increase p99 TTFT by ~10-20% in our experience.
- We recommend an additional soak with mixed long- and short-contexts to validate the p99 tail.

Attachment: benchmark_results_qc.csv
